name: Dithered-edge wipe

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-5, 2026-11-27): a particle-built product intro wipes from its dark opening to an ivory scene behind a leading edge of dithered grain.

technique: A wipe from a dark scene to a light one whose leading edge is a soft band of dithered grain, so the change reads as print or particles turning over rather than a hard line. It suits films built from dots or print texture.
purpose: Change from dark to light with an edge that belongs to a print or particle look, instead of a clean line.
visual_behaviour: A vertical edge crosses left to right in about a third of a second; the edge is a soft band of light dots thinning into the dark; the incoming headline is already in place under it.
mechanics: A vertical edge crosses left to right in about 0.35 s; the edge is a band about 15-20% of the width of light dots thinning into the dark; the incoming headline is already in place under it.

parameters.name: band_width
parameters.description: dithered band, share of the width

use_cases: Dark-to-light act changes in particle or print-texture films

implementation.approach: Studio.fx.wipe from the left (about 0.35 s) for the clip, with the hard edge replaced by a band about 18% of the width filled with a seeded dot pattern (Studio.rng, drawn once to a canvas and used as a CSS mask on the incoming layer), so every render is identical. The dithered mask is not built.

priority.note: One use in the corpus; kept as its own record because the mechanism (a noise-masked moving edge) differs from bars (random-bar-wipe) and from a striped band (diagonal-band-wipe).

provenance.observed: A grain-edged wipe crosses from the left, dark to ivory, in about 0.35 s (7.50-7.85 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
